{"text": "Thanks for the detailed report — this is a clean diagnosis.

One small note on the title: the traceback actually shows a `yaml.scanner.ScannerError` (the BOM byte sequence decodes to `U+FEFF`, which YAML then rejects as "a character that cannot start any token"), not a `UnicodeDecodeError`. Either way, the root cause is exactly what you identified: `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` keeps the BOM in the decoded string, and PyYAML chokes on it.

Switching to `encoding="utf-8-sig"` is the right fix here: it transparently strips a leading BOM when present and is otherwise identical to `utf-8`, so it's safe for existing BOM-less config files too. That's the standard way to handle this on Windows, where Notepad and other editors routinely write a UTF-8 BOM.

A PR with that one-line change would be very welcome. If you send one, it'd be nice (but not required) to include a small regression test — e.g. write a temp YAML file starting with `\ufeff` and assert `load_config()` returns the expected dict. Thanks! 👍"}
